messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 triggered: high 5xx rate from EU edge -> smart-routing fallbacks. Alert: PD#12345. Impact: ~12 customers experiencing generation failures or extreme latency :rotating_light:
maya: I'm on it. Paging rotation -> sam (EU oncall) :phone:
sam: grabbing pager, joining. any initial customer reports?
support-ops: ACME, BrightPay, and two internal e2e tests failing. Tickets opened.
maya: logs show lots of 502/504 from gateway-routes in eu-west. But origin responses look healthy when hit directly. suspect edge/DNS.
alex: seeing abnormal routing policy: many requests being routed to `model-variant: gpt-small-quant` in us-east fallback instead of `gpt-medium-v2` in eu; policy eval shows fallback triggered due to stale edge endpoint health check failures.
priya: can you paste the routing policy snippet?
alex: here's the relevant policy snippet from prod config (sanitized):
```
route: smart-region
  preferred_region: eu-west
  fallback_regions: [us-east, us-west]
  variant_priority: [gpt-medium-v2, gpt-small-quant]
  health_check: endpoint: eu-1.edge.redwood.net
  health_check_ttl: 300
  fallback_on_health_fail: true
```
sam: hmm health_check endpoint eu-1.edge.redwood.net resolves to an old CNAME that's been removed from the eu pool. Looks like DNS entry was updated during a previous migration but TTL stayed high.
maya: can you show `dig` and `curl` from our lib-diagnostics box?
alex: pasted outputs below from `lib-diag-eu1` (cut):
```
$ dig +short eu-1.edge.redwood.net
203.0.113.45  # old IP (us-east backfill)
$ curl -sS -D - https://eu-1.edge.redwood.net/health -o /dev/null | head
HTTP/2 200
content-length: 0
x-edge-region: us-east  <-- WRONG
```
priya: that confirms DNS stale mapping -> health checks report OK but to wrong region, so smart-routing marks eu as unhealthy and falls back to us variant (which also mismatched priority and led to small quant).
sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) update routing policy to disable `fallback_on_health_fail` temporarily, 2) change health_check endpoint to a stable eu host, 3) update DNS CNAMEs to point to correct eu pool and reduce TTL, 4) add explicit route pin for high-value customers.
emily: I'm writing a short customer-facing blurb for impacted customers. Need ETA for fix.
maya: short-term: I'll push a policy override to disable fallback on health_fail (quick revertable). then update DNS via Cloudflare API to correct CNAME and lower TTL to 30s.
sam: agree. I'll run the DNS change and trigger CDN cache purge. Steps:
- `curl -X PATCH https://api.cloudflare.com/... -d '{"content":"eu.pool.redwood.net"}'`
- `curl -X POST https://api.cloudflare.com/.../purge_cache`
- verify with `dig +trace` and `curl -I` from lib-diag boxes.
maya: doing policy override now. applying: `redwoodctl routes update smart-region --set fallback_on_health_fail=false --env prod`
incident-bot: Deploy bot: route config update started by maya (deploy-req 7891).
(some minutes)
alex: policy override applied. route eval shows no more automatic fallback triggered for eu. Traffic should stick to preferred region.
sam: DNS change submitted to CF; purge requested. Monitoring propagation...
sam: verification from three e2e agents: `dig eu-1.edge.redwood.net -> 198.51.100.12` (correct eu IP).
priya: re-running load tests -> error rate dropping back to baseline.
emily: sending customers short update: "We're mitigating an edge routing issue — fallbacks caused mismatched model variants. We've applied a policy override and corrected DNS; continued monitoring."
support-ops: posted update to ACME ticket and scheduled follow-up call at +30m.
maya: next step: create a durable fix: replace health_check host with an authoritative eu-only health endpoint and lower DNS TTLs before next migration. Add an automated DNS check in the routing policy CI.
sam: also recommend adding an explicit mapping in the smart-router for critical customers to avoid fallback during migrations.
priya: capturing timeline for postmortem. can someone add exact timestamps and commands used?
alex: added to the incident doc (internal link in case notes). PD#12345 updated with actions and owner tags.
incident-bot: All hands: incident status -> mitigated. severity: P1 -> reduced to P2 for root-cause investigation. next oncall: sam handing to maya for postmortem.
maya: handoff to sam for postmortem write-up. I'll remain available for followups. :white_check_mark:
sam: I will own RCA. initial customer impact: 12 customers, average 4–6 minute degraded generation or wrong model variant for up to ~15 minutes during migration windows.
emily: I'll prepare the customer digest and include mitigation steps and ETA for RCA.
priya: action items assigned:
- alex: implement health_check endpoint change + CI test (owner: alex)
- sam: DNS migration playbook + lower TTL preflight (owner: sam)
- maya: add critical-customer explicit route config (owner: maya)
- emily: customer communications (owner: emily)
- support-ops: coordinate post-incident customer calls (owner: support-ops)

sam: closing notes: PD#12345 will remain open until postmortem published. Thanks everyone for quick mitigation.
incident-bot: Reaction summary: :rotating_light: -> raised, :white_check_mark: -> mitigated. Incident thread closed for live updates; continue in postmortem doc.
